$schemaComment: Reviewed NuGet package-signing certificate fingerprints used to pin `dotnet nuget verify --all --certificate-fingerprint ...` for the anchor packages (SkiaSharp, SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz, HarfBuzzSharp). SkiaSharp packages carry both an author signature (Microsoft Corporation) and a repository signature (NuGet.org); --all verifies every signature present, so both roles must be represented here or verification of a dual-signed package would fail. Design for additive rotation: when a certificate is renewed, add the new fingerprint and keep the old one (do not remove it) so packages already signed with it keep verifying; only remove an entry after confirming no anchor package still carries that signature. validUntil is the certificate's own validity end (informational/audit only): an expired signing certificate does not invalidate packages already signed with it (NuGet timestamps the signature), so verification never filters by validUntil at runtime.
